doesNotClaim: A Bell test measures entanglement — the EPR side. It does not measure spacetime geometry.

ER=EPR is established in a specific holographic model (two entangled systems describing a two-sided black hole in AdS). Extending the geometric picture to ordinary entangled particles remains conjectural.
Google's Sycamore 2022 experiment simulated a holographic wormhole model's teleportation signature on a 9-qubit circuit. It measured quantum circuit behavior, not a wormhole or spacetime.
The geometric half — a derivation or measurement linking entanglement to geometry outside the AdS model — is the open part.

alreadyAligned: RFC 8785 canonical JSON is byte-order-neutral (UTF-8 text, keys sorted).
endianness.enforcedBy: tests/numina-protocol-pqc.test.mjs (hybrid bundle length-prefix is big-endian; a little-endian-encoded bundle is rejected) and tests/numina-protocol-kex.test.mjs (transcript length prefixes are big-endian).
labeledExceptions: Ed25519 field elements and scalars are little-endian per RFC 8032 — the primitive's own encoding, never re-encoded.
ML-KEM and ML-DSA byte encodings are exactly as NIST FIPS 203 / FIPS 204 define them — never re-encoded.
Re-encoding any primitive's internal bytes would break verification and interoperability; the big-endian rule governs only layouts defined by this protocol.
endianness.rule: Big-endian (network byte order) everywhere in every byte layout defined by the Singularity Protocol: canonical JSON serialization, length prefixes, version and algorithm fields, the hybrid signature bundle layout, and the key-exchange transcript. A decoder MUST interpret multi-byte integers as big-endian and MUST reject a layout whose length prefixes do not parse as big-endian.

cryptoAgility.note: A future algorithm lands by a version bump of this section (schema) plus new pinned keys — not by redesigning the record format. The classical Ed25519 layer is retained alongside every PQC layer (hybrid, never PQC-only), so a break in either layer alone does not silently void verification.

hybridKeyExchange.construction: Initiator generates an ephemeral X25519 keypair and computes the X25519 shared secret (32 bytes) with the responder's X25519 public key; encapsulates to the responder's ML-KEM-768 public key (ciphertext 1,088 bytes, shared secret 32 bytes). IKM = X25519 shared secret (32 bytes) || ML-KEM-768 shared secret (32 bytes), X25519 first. HKDF-SHA-256 with salt UTF-8('numina-pqc-kex-v1') and info UTF-8(the profile string) derives 32 bytes = the AES-256-GCM key. Transcript (returned for the caller to bind/sign) = UTF-8(profile) || 0x00 || uint32-BE length + initiator ephemeral X25519 SPKI DER || uint32-BE length + responder X25519 SPKI DER || uint32-BE length + ML-KEM-768 ciphertext. Authentication of the transcript is by hybrid signature (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65) and is the caller's responsibility; the KEX module itself does not sign.
hybridKeyExchange.keyEncoding: X25519 public keys are SPKI DER hex (44 bytes); ML-KEM-768 public keys are SPKI DER hex (1,206 bytes = 22-byte prefix + 1,184-byte raw public key).
hybridKeyExchange.supersedesProfileNameOnly: numina-e2ee-x25519-hkdf-aes256gcm-ed25519-v1 (named in AGENTS.md only; no code implemented it, so nothing is migrated and the old name is never reused for this different construction).

hybridSignature.bundleLayout: Binary bundle, 3,383 bytes total: ASCII magic 'NPQ1' (4 bytes) || version uint16 big-endian = 1 || Ed25519 length uint16 big-endian = 64 || Ed25519 signature (64 bytes) || ML-DSA-65 length uint16 big-endian = 3309 || ML-DSA-65 signature (3,309 bytes). All length prefixes are big-endian (see the top-level endianness rule). No truncation, no compression.
hybridSignature.keyEncoding: ML-DSA-65 public keys are stored as SPKI DER hex (1,974 bytes = 22-byte SPKI prefix + 1,952-byte raw public key).
hybridSignature.whatIsSigned: The SAME RFC 8785 canonical bytes are signed twice: once with Ed25519 (64-byte signature) and once with ML-DSA-65 (3,309-byte signature). Verification requires BOTH signatures to verify over the same canonical bytes; either failing — or a missing ML-DSA-65 key — fails the whole verification. Existing single-Ed25519 records still verify through the unchanged verifySignature path.
